# ATM: An Active-Detection Trust Mechanism for VANETs Based on Blockchain
Fuliang Li, Zhenbei Guo, Changsheng Zhang, Weichao Li, Yi Wang · IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology 2021 · https://doi.org/10.1109/tvt.2021.3050007 · relevance: medium · basis: abstract

**Problem:** Existing trust mechanisms in vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) suffer from a variety of vulnerabilities, such as trust inconsistency in different regions and fake trust values generated by a set of cooperating malicious nodes. In this paper, we propose a novel local trust management mechanism, ATM, to solve these problems.
**Approach:** In this paper, we propose a novel local trust management mechanism, ATM, to solve these problems. We conduct numerical analysis to evaluate the performance of ATM.
**Tools and scale:** Not stated in the abstract.
**Results:** Our experiment results show that ATM performs the best among the three trust mechanisms under test. It can effectively identify malicious behaviors in terms of 95% detection accuracy and 90% deliver ratio, respectively.
**Limitations and future work (as stated by the authors):**
- None stated in the abstract.
**Overlap with our engine:** partial — Trust/reputation management for detecting malicious senders; an alternative to the SCMS misbehaviour-report -> MA -> CRL pipeline our engine models, with no linkage-based revocation or time-to-neutralise analysis.
**Novelty implications:** Does not rule out any candidate direction; it does not model SCMS certificates, linkage-based revocation, per-message joint ground truth or counterfactual reruns.
